note: Dates when something must be re-checked (a decision announced, a pending case, a periodic review). check-watch.mjs lists the items whose date has passed; in CI it opens one GitHub issue per item. When an item is handled: update the legal files, then move its date forward or delete it.

items.title: BGH judgment in LAION (I ZR 281/25), announced for 2026-12-17
items.what: Read the BGH press release and the judgment: is a natural-language TDM reservation in terms of use 'machine-readable' (§ 44b(3) UrhG)? Does § 60d cover the dataset?

items.title: Thomson Reuters v. Ross, Third Circuit (No. 25-2153, 2026-09-30): read the disposition
items.what: The opinion was only partly read: confirm whether the district court was affirmed on copyrightability and fair use.

items.title: Bartz v. Anthropic: final approval of the class settlement?
items.what: Check the docket for the final approval order after the preliminary approval of 2025-10-17.

items.title: CJEU C-250/25 Like Company v Google: Advocate General opinion or judgment?
items.what: Check whether an AG opinion (CELEX 62025CC0250) or a judgment (62025CJ0250) has been published; question 3 is about Article 4 of Directive 2019/790 and LLM training.

items.title: IETF aipref: has a vocabulary or attachment RFC been published?
items.what: A published RFC (robots.txt extension or header for AI usage preferences) would need code in check-robots.mjs or check-page.mjs and a new signal.

items.title: Quarterly legal review (EU, FR, DE, UK, US)
items.what: Re-read every source in sources.md marked by hand (Légifrance, leginfo), look for new laws, decisions and guidance (CNIL, ICO, EDPB, Copyright Office, UK government), update the 'Last checked' dates, release a patch version with a 'Legal update' CHANGELOG entry. Then move this date three months forward.
